text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A prosecutor investigating a car crash which linked an MP, a police official and a gangster describes it as a gangland case because drugs, arms and silencers were found in the car.
- Conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz confirms that his house is bugged and says he has been threatened.
- Islamist deputy Aydin Menderes, whose father censored the press when he was prime minister, calls on the government not to repeat the mistake.
- The MP involved in the car crash scandal, Sedat Bucak, confirms to the far-rightist newspaper Gozcu that all arms in the car were his, but denies owning silencers found there.
- Six of MP Bucak's bodyguards are questioned by a state security court prosecutor.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's call for duty free trade between Moslem countries is unrealistic.
- Prime Minister Erbakan calls for Moslem states to invest in Turkey at a meeting with Moslem businessmen.
- Journalist Ugur Dundar says he was exposed to the threat of assassination because Tansu Ciller's family pressured the chief of police to withdraw his official bodyguards.
- Amnesty International protests against torture in police custody in Turkey.
- Three audio surveillance devices are found in the main opposition leader's house.
